descriptionChirho: The physical corner, angle, or turning-point of a building, altar, wall, street, or city fortification; includes singular, plural, construct, and suffixed forms referring to spatial corners.

A corner-stone (אֶבֶן פִּנָּה) or chief foundation stone, used both literally of architecture and metaphorically of God's creative or redemptive work (Psalm 118:22, Job 38:6, Isaiah 28:16, Zechariah 10:4).
Figurative use of 'corner' to denote a leader, chief, or pillar of the community, as in the 'corners of the people' (פִּנּוֹת הָעָם) meaning the chiefs or principal men (Judges 20:2, 1 Samuel 14:38).
